children: Palo Alto Networks saw a decline of 5.24%, closing at $362.09. The stock hit a high of $375.92 and a low of $357.26 during the day, with a 52-week range of $398.87 to $139.57. The shares dropped 1.9% to $355.20.

Palo Alto Networks reported fourth-quarter revenue of $3.41 billion, up 34% year over year and above the $3.35 billion analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of $1.02 topped expectations of 98 cents. The company guided for fiscal 2027 revenue of $14.10 billion-$14.20 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.16-$4.19, both above Wall Street estimates, and announced the acquisition of AI-native platform Console.

Credo Technology’s stock dropped 8.65% to $206.63, with an intraday high of $221.74 and a low of $206.12. The 52-week range is $308.67 to $86.49. In after-hours trading, the stock fell sharply by 10.15% to $185.65

Credo Technology reported first-quarter revenue of approximately $479 million, up 114.7% year over year and 9.6% sequentially, beating the $471.77 million analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of $1.20 topped expectations of $1.17. The company guided for second-quarter revenue of $525 million-$535 million, above the $515.79 million estimate, and forecast adjusted gross margin of 67%-69%.

MongoDB’s shares fell 4.23%, ending at $434.21. The stock’s high and low were $448.68 and $430.53, respectively, with a 52-week range of $473.1 to $215.68. The stock crashed 13.94% to $373.70 in extended trading.

MongoDB reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $771.77 million, up 30% year over year and above the $732.91 million analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of $1.90 beat expectations of $1.61. The company raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.39-$6.58 from $6.11 and revenue outlook to $2.99 billion-$3.03 billion from $2.95 billion.

GitLab’s stock decreased by 3.12%, closing at $45.09. The day’s high was $46.38, and the low was $44.46, with a 52-week range of $52.38 to $18.73. In the after-hours trading, the stock shot up 17.32% to $52.90.

GitLab reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $286.25 million, up from $235.96 million a year earlier and above the $273.12 million analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of 24 cents topped expectations of 18 cents. The company raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance to 85-87 cents from 81 cents and revenue outlook to $1.129 billion-$1.133 billion from $1.12 billion.
